What the model says

Across 232 qualified MLB hitters in 2026, at equal swing length, contact and whiff rate, +1 mph of bat speed is associated with +10 points of xwOBA, and +1 point of squared-up rate with +4 points. The swing metrics explain 42% of the differences in production between hitters; adding swing decisions (chase and in-zone swing rates) raises it to 47%. The rest comes from timing, launch direction and factors public data does not capture.

These are cross-sectional associations, not guarantees: they set the hypothesis to test with the player, not the expected outcome.

Development plan

Diagnosis. Daulton Varsho already generates above-average bat speed (72.9 mph, 60th percentile), but his contact quality (16th percentile in squared-up rate) and whiff rate (62nd percentile) limit how much of that speed turns into damage.

Priority. Convert speed into quality contact.

  1. Screen – Swing length, attack angle and path vs pitch location; timing.
  2. Intervene – Constraint-based drills for a more efficient path; timing work.
  3. Monitor – Squared-up and whiff rates each week, with bat speed protected.
Reference points – similar bat speed, better contact

Percentiles (1–100), model and profiles are based on the 232 qualified MLB hitters in 2026 (570+ competitive swings). Profiles: k-means on bat speed, swing length, squared-up and whiff rates.
